title.narrative: Energy Sector Development Investment Program - Tranche 3

description.narrative:
The government requested ADB to finance the Gereshk Electricity Services Improvement Project. Gereshk, with a population of approximately 70,000, is a district economic center in Helmand province in soutern Afghanistan, where insurgency has been significantly active. Gereshk is strategically located on the national highway (Corridor 1) that connects Herat to Kandahar. With the stability being regained, the government would like to restore the licit livelihood of the town residents and functions of the town as the district economic center. However, the rehabilitation and expansion of the existing hydropower plant is needed to make more power available in Gereshk. Upgrading and expansion of electricity distribution infrastructure and end-user connections are likewise necessary to increase the access to electricity. In addition, enhancement of DABS' capacity is required to implement the project and improve operation and maintenance of the system.
The impact of the project will be better power supply in areas south of Kabul. The project will increase access to more reliable power supply in Gereshk. The project outcome will be increased hydropower generation capacity in Gereshk.
The project will rehabilitate and upgrade the Gereshk power supply system. It will increase household connections from 2,500 to 5,000 covering 50,000 people residing within the 6 km radius of the town center. With increased installed generation capacity and upgraded distribution system, the project will improved the access to more stable electricity.
The project will include the following components to improve and expand the Gereshk distribution system and strengthen DABS operational capacity. Physical component of the project will include: (i) rehabilitation and upgrading of hydropower plant with 4.8 MW installation capacity; (ii) replacement of 10 km of 3.3 kV distribution lines to 20 kV line; and (iii) replacement and new installation of end-user meters. Non-physical component will enhance DABS project implementation and operation and maintenance capacities.
Increase in hydropower generation capacity in Gereshk

Available power supply load increased from 1.2 MW (2009) to 4.5 MW by 2014 Achievement: 1 Progress/Status: The civil work contract including rehabilitation of powerhouse infrastructure and replacement of 3 hydro-turbines is completed on 22 October 2020. During the project implementation, there was deteriorated security in the Helmand province/project site and also a weak performance by the contractor, the project has faced further delays; therefore, EA has requested ADB for another 1.5 years extension to this grant and ADB approved the extension till 30 June 2018. The contractor was not able to complete the work, and EA requested a further extension of the grant from 1 July 2018 to 28 November 2018. The grant closing date was further extended from 28 May 2020 to 28 November 2020 to complete the remaining works. The work is 100% completed as of 28 November 2020 and the project is physically closed.
The winding-up period of the project was extended from 31 December 2023 and then till 31 December 2026 to process and allow the final payment to the contractor and financially close the project. As per the approved approach paper “Afghanistan 2021 Situation: Proposed Actions and Next Steps” ADB has paused its operations. Data Source: DABS Gereshk power system statistic report
Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: 3. DABS' operational capacity increased Indicator: 100 DABS staff to gain experience in the installation works of the distribution system by 2013 Achievement: 1 Progress/Status: Achieved. DABS operational and PMO staff have received formal and informal on-job training by ADB financed consultants from SMEC, Hill International, and Individual consultants, and contractors working on distribution rehabilitation projects (AIPL-HUNAN, KEC, FEKA, CNEEC-MAMMAR).
In tranche 3, the supervision consultancy services contract with Hill International was signed in Q1 2013 and the contract was completed in December 2016. Six individual consultants were recruited from January 2017 until May 2020. Out of six consultants, the three individual consultant contracts were extended from 28 May 2020 to 28 November 2020 to monitor project works and provide support and capacity building to DABS staff. Data Source: DABS Project Progress Reports

The contract value was increased by 29% from the original contract value from $4.44 million to $5.738 million. The completion of the work was expected by the end of Q4 2016 but due to deteriorated security in Helmand province/project site and also a weak performance by the contractor the project has faced was delayed, therefore, EA has requested ADB for 1.5 years extension to grant and ADB approved the extension till 30 June 2018. The work is 100% completed as of 28 November 2020 and the project is physically closed.
